10.1002_adfm.202514936: The successful commercialization of direct ethanol fuel cells (DEFCs) hinges on the development of highly efficient electrocatalysts capable of overcoming key performance limitations. In this study, the core–shell Au@Pd pentatwinned decahedral nanoparticles has been synthesized with controlled Pd shell thicknesses, varying in the average number of Pd monolayers over the Au core. This core‐shell configuration promotes the epitaxial growth of Pd atoms with varying degrees of tensile strain. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that increasing tensile strain shifts the d‐band center closer to the Fermi level. Notably, when the Pd shell is three monolayers, the upward shift of the d‐band center is maximum, and this further amplified by the ligand effect from the underlying Au core. The synergistic influence of five twin boundaries, tensile strain, and ligand interactions collectively tunes the d‐band center, resulting in the Au@Pd‐3 catalyst achieving an exceptional mass activity of 25.67 A mg Pd −1 and a specific activity of 21.30 mA cm −2 , representing enhancements of 38.31‐fold and 11.39‐fold, respectively, over commercial Pd/C. This study highlights how the combined effects of strain and ligand interactions can be strategically harnessed to design high‐performance electrocatalysts by tuning the position of d‐band center.
10.1002_adfm.78340: The performance of wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite sub‐cells in tandem solar cells is largely constrained by grain boundary and surface defects, along with unfavorable interfacial energy level alignment. To address these issues, we propose a bilayer co‐ligand post‐treatment strategy, initially employing 3‐(methylthio)propylamine hydroiodide (3MTPAI) and 1, 3‐propanediamine dihydroiodide (PDAI 2 ), followed by a secondary piperazinium iodide (PI) layer. In this design, 3MTPAI penetrates the grain boundaries to passivate both grain boundary and surface defects, thereby suppressing non‐radiative recombination, while PDAI 2 forms an initial surface dipole layer to enhance the built‐in electric field. The subsequent PI layer not only passivates residual defects but also generates a second dipole layer that acts synergistically with the first, facilitating carrier transport at the interface. Consequently, the optimized WBG (1.68 eV) single‐junction and tandem devices achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 23.55% and 32.33%, respectively, and show no efficiency loss after 500 h of operation. This work demonstrates that the bilayer co‐ligand strategy offers valuable insights for developing efficient and stable single‐junction and tandem solar cells.
10.1002_adfm.78919: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a bottleneck for water electrolysis, remains limited by the adsorbate scaling relations and sluggish interfacial electron transfer (IET). We address these challenges by anchoring mixed‐valence Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ motifs on aspartic‐acid–derived carbon dots (AspCDs). Spectroscopic analyses support trinuclear Fe 3 sites, which offer redox flexibility and proximal active centers. The Fe 3 site binds the substrate (OH − ) and is electronically coupled to the AspCD scaffold. Together with the work function‐aligned scaffold for electron abstraction from OH − , these features establish effective inner‐sphere IET from OH − , through the active Fe 3 center and the AspCDs host to the electrode. Simultaneously, the mixed valency buffers the charge build‐up during the successive proton‐coupled electron transfers. The catalyst drives fast and selective O 2 generation and minimizes H 2 O 2 formation, while sustaining at least ∼70 h of continuous operation with a gradual ∼90 mV total potential increase. Thus, the Fe 3 /AspCDs catalyst requires only 110 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm −2 , shows particularly effective kinetics with a low Tafel slope of 41 mV dec −1 , and has a turnover frequency of 2.1 s −1 . The design integrates crucial physicochemical properties for highly efficient OER, and the principle can be generalized to other systems toward further advances in the field.
10.1002_anie.202518760: The development of lithium–sulfur (Li−S) batteries is hindered by the polysulfide dissolving, cross‐over and the inherent lithium metal anode instability. We herein instead describe a lithiated silicon−sulfur (LiSi−S) battery enabled by molecular engineering of highly solvating nitrile electrolytes toward weakly solvating to fundamentally decouple the reactions of the two electrodes and eliminate their cross‐talk. Specifically, by controlled fluorination of the ethoxy‐nitrile base solvent, the charge distribution on the solvent is manipulated which suppresses the solvation for polysulfides promoting a quasi‐solid‐state sulfur reaction (QSSSR) mechanism. The promoted anion participation in Li + solvation, along with the fluoroethylene carbonate additive, further stabilizes the interphases at both sulfur cathode and LiSi anode mitigating the mechanical degradations. The QSSSR‐based LiSi−S cell shows a high capacity of 1499.0 mA h g sulfur −1 at 0.1C, and achieves a high capacity retention of 90.2% over 100 cycles at 0.2C with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%. This work highlights the essence of molecular engineering for manipulating the primary reactions and interphasial behaviors at both electrodes toward high performance sulfur batteries.
10.1002_smll.73129: Capacitive deionization (CDI) emerges as a promising low‐energy desalination technology to address global water scarcity. However, its performance hinges on the design of advanced electrode materials. Herein, we proposed a novel strategy to prepare the yolk‐shell structured transition metal phosphides/hollow mesoporous carbon spheres (HMCSs) composites (HZNP). The unique hollow interior effectively accommodates volume variation during ion intercalation/deintercalation. Meanwhile, the mesoporous carbon shell offers a high specific surface area and continuous pathways for ion diffusion, thereby synergistically improving charge transfer kinetics and structural stability. The HZNP‐20‐30 composite demonstrates an optimal desalination capacity of 49.6 mg g −1 . This performance is attributable to its preserved ZIF framework from ion‐exchange etching, which maintains chemical and structural integrity. Furthermore, the synergistic effect between the CoNi bimetallic phosphides and the N‐doped mesoporous carbon shell significantly enhances the electrochemical performance. This study not only provides strong theoretical support for the confined growth of metal phosphide nanoparticles in HMCSs but also verifies the superiority of the yolk‐shell structure in the application of CDI.
10.1021_acs.analchem.6c04473: The single-signal multistate conversion sensing mode not only improves detection sensitivity but also features a simple construction process and can effectively eliminate nonspecific signal interferences. The change of molecular structure and generation of new molecules are able to regulate the activation and inhibition of the resonance energy transfer (RET) mechanism more easily through the conversion of energy levels, thus realizing the on-off-on mode. In this work, a controlled release strategy was used to trigger the self-assembly of Bi2S3/BiOI heterojunctions via the release of Na2S, resulting from the specific recognition between carbohydrate antigen 242 (CA242) and its antibody. The formation of the Bi2S3/BiOI heterojunction changed the energy level of BiOI, thereby inhibiting the RET mechanism between the [Ru(dcbpy)3]Cl2 hydrogel (Ru-Hydrogel) and BiOI, and restoring the signal, achieving the on-off-on mode of the sensor. It was an effective method to directly relate the concentration of the target CA242 (10-4-103 U/mL) to the multistate conversion of the signal. The limit of detection of this sensor for CA242 reached 1.57 × 10-4 U/mL (S/N = 3), demonstrating high sensitivity. This study provided an innovative sensing strategy for fabricating electrochemiluminescence sensors in the on-off-on mode and offered a feasible method for the high-sensitivity detection of biomarkers in the analysis field.
10.1021_acscatal.6c05377: Atomically dispersed metal catalysts demonstrate significant catalytic potential, though achieving precise structural elucidation and electronic modulation remains a key challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis and characterization of three isostructural, semiconducting heterometallic titanium-oxo clusters, Ti14M2(μ3-O)13(μ2-O)8(H2O)(C6H5CO2)18(Nfm)3 (designated as Ti14M2, where M2 = CoNi, Co2, or Ni2), serving as molecularly precise model systems for dual single-atom catalysts. Distinct electronic interaction between the heterometallic Co and Ni sites in Ti14CoNi modulates the local charge distribution, lowering the charge density at Ni while elevating it at Co. In photocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), Ti14CoNi exhibits high performance, ranking among the best catalysts, surpassing Ti14Co2 and Ti14Ni2, as well as many state-of-the-art solid-state Ni, Fe, Cu, and Co single atom catalysts. Notably, Ti14CoNi retains activity even when using simulated flue gas as the CO2 source. Experimental and DFT studies reveal that Ni acts as the primary catalytic site for CO2RR in Ti14CoNi, with *COOH formation as the rate-determining step, while the lowered Ni valence state enhances CO2 activation and suppresses H2 evolution. The dual-metal strategy improves CO2RR efficiency and provides a thermodynamically favorable pathway for CO production. Our findings establish molecular metal-oxo clusters as atomically precise dual single atom catalysts and offer valuable insights for developing efficient CO2RR catalysts of the next generation.
10.1038_s41467-026-78721-4: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. OH AWCs mediated the transport pathways, enabling the membrane to deliver a NaCl rejection of 99.2 ± 0.3%, an NDMA rejection of 93.9 ± 0.1% that surpassed the existing upper bound of permselectivity, and an ultrahigh pure water permeance (4.5 ± 0.2 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1) that exceeded that of state-of-the-art RO membranes. Within the OH AWCs, the hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules and the -OH resulted in a short residence time and a high jump frequency of water molecules, enabling the formation of dynamic and continuous OH-H2O networks that facilitated rapid water movement. In contrast, NaCl and NDMA faced high trans-channel energy barriers, which significantly hindered their transport through the OH AWCs. The resulting AWCM membrane outperforms prevailing RO membranes and offers valuable insights for the design of next-generation RO membranes. Low N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) rejection by reverse osmosis membrane threatens the quality of permeate. Here, the authors created a membrane with hydroxy artificial water channels, improving water permeance and NDMA rejection for safer water reuse.

10.1109_tdei.2026.3739730: Polymer-based thin-film capacitors are vital for advanced capacitive energy storage, but face high-temperature limits due to degraded breakdown strength (Eb) and increased leakage current. Poly(m-phenylene isophthalamide) (PMIA), featuring a high intrinsic dielectric constant (εr), serves as a promising candidate for insulation improvement. HfO2nanoparticles, featuring large bandgap and high εr, are incorporated as reinforcing fillers to prepare the PMIA/HfO2composite films by electrospinning. HfO2serves as a dual-functional filler: it increases theEbof composite films by suppressing leakage current, which stems from both its own superior insulation and the formation of interfacial traps due to a high interfacial energy barrier of 1.71 eV; it also enhances dielectric polarization via the Maxwell-Wagner-Sillars effect. Consequently, the optimized 0.5 wt% PMIA/HfO2film exhibits an improvedEbof 663.8 kV/mm at 150 °C and 606.5 kV/mm at 200 °C, along with enhanced εrvalues of 5.40 and 5.62 at 100 Hz, respectively. These enable a maximum energy density of 12.32 J/cm3at 150 °C and 10.95 J/cm3at 200 °C, representing increases of 130.7% and 458.7%, compared to the pure PMIA film. Furthermore, it exhibits stable cyclic charge-discharge performance, offering a feasible strategy for developing high-performance dielectrics for high-temperature energy storage applications.
